title: Drag a template onto the canvas
summary: Drag a template onto the canvas | Click and hold a template, then drop it on the canvas to add the screen. Double-click the new node to open the Screen Editor and configure it.

title: Search for a screen type
summary: Search for a screen type | Type to filter templates by name or description; the list updates as you type. Clear the field to see all templates.

title: Open the Screen Templates panel
summary: Open the Screen Templates panel | The right sidebar lists draggable screen templates with previews and is always visible. It is the primary way to add new screens to the canvas.

title: Choose screen types intentionally
summary: Choose screen types intentionally | Question screens collect answers into variables for routing, content screens explain value, embed screens host custom HTML, and paywall screens sell products. Pick by what each step should accomplish.

title: Screen names stay unique automatically
summary: Screen names stay unique automatically | When you add a screen whose type already exists, the system appends a number (for example Hero Content 2). This keeps analytics and navigation unambiguous.

title: Find the connection ports
summary: Find the connection ports | Each node has handles on its edges: input handles on the left of non-launch screens, and one output handle per action on the right. Hover a handle to see its action label.

title: Draw a default connection
summary: Draw a default connection | Drag from an output handle on the source to an input handle on the target to create an edge. This is an unconditional path: every visitor who takes that action goes to the target.

title: Remove a connection
summary: Remove a connection | Click an edge, then Delete Connection and confirm. The target becomes unreachable through that action unless another path exists.

title: Add conditions to a connection
summary: Add conditions to a connection | Click an edge to open Connection Details, then Edit Conditions to define AND/OR logic on flow variables. Conditional paths activate only when the conditions are true.

summary: FlexibleLayout sections add their own handles | FlexibleLayout screens hold multiple sections (content, buttons, options, embeds, paywalls), and each can generate its own connection handles. Handles appear automatically based on the sections you add.

title: Verify the flow is complete
summary: Verify the flow is complete | Before publishing, confirm a launch screen is set, every non-final screen has an outgoing connection, paywall screens point to valid products, and each branch ends meaningfully.

title: Use the toolbar controls

title: Read the flow structure

title: Identify the launch screen
summary: Identify the launch screen | The first screen carries a First screen label on its left. The launch screen is where every visitor enters; only one can be the launch screen and it cannot have incoming connections.

title: Navigate the canvas
summary: Navigate the canvas | Scroll to zoom, hold space and drag to pan, and use the minimap in the corner for the full layout. Click to select a screen; Ctrl+click to multi-select.

title: Focus field when screen loads
summary: Focus field when screen loads | When enabled, the field automatically receives focus and opens the keyboard when the screen appears. Default is true. Useful for primary input fields.

summary: Connect Stripe before adding products | Click Connect to link your Stripe account here first — Segmently needs it to match each paywall product to a real Stripe product and price so payments actually go through. Stripe's Test and Live environments are separate accounts, so each…

title: Start from the onboarding list

title: Name and organize the draft
summary: Name and organize the draft | Give the draft a clear internal name — this is just for you to find it in the list, and visitors never see it. Optionally drop it in a folder to keep a long list tidy. Keep one draft per ad campaign instead of making duplicates, because separate…

title: Set the default language
summary: Set the default language | The default language is the fallback locale used when a visitor has no matching localized content. Choose the primary audience language.

title: Optionally assign a folder
summary: Optionally assign a folder | Choose a folder to organize the draft in the Onboardings list, or leave it at the root level. The folder only affects organization and can be changed later.

title: Add supported languages
summary: Add supported languages | Add every locale you intend to publish so screens can carry localized copy from the start. You can extend this later, but planning it now avoids rework.

title: Name the onboarding
summary: Name the onboarding | Use a clear internal name so the draft is easy to find in the Onboardings list. The name is not shown to visitors.

title: Choose the platform
summary: Choose the platform | The platform controls the publish surface and runtime behavior. Web flows publish through Web Placement; pick it before selecting a theme.

title: Configure the action buttons
summary: Configure the action buttons | These are the buttons at the bottom of each screen — a primary one (usually 'Continue') and an optional secondary one. Set whether each is shown, its label style, and its look. Their colors pull from your Titles & Subtitles and Button Title theme…

title: Set the background
summary: Set the background | Choose a solid color, a photo, or a video clip to sit behind every screen. Whatever you pick must keep headings, body text, and buttons easy to read — low contrast here hurts conversion on every single screen, so favor a calm background over a busy one.

title: Set the color scheme

title: Create the onboarding
summary: Create the onboarding | Click Create to apply this theme and generate the draft. Everything you set here is just a starting point — you can still override the colors, fonts, and layout on any individual screen later in the Screen Editor.

title: Choose fonts and text styling
summary: Choose fonts and text styling | Main Font Family is the base font used for all text. You can give Titles and Subtitles their own family, weight, size, color, and alignment if you want them to stand out. Your font choices flow into option cards, product cards, and every screen,…

title: Configure the header bar
summary: Configure the header bar | The header bar sits at the top of every screen. Toggle the back button, the skip button, and the progress indicator on or off. Leaving the progress indicator on reassures visitors how far along they are, which helps them finish; colors and fonts here…

title: Review the live preview
summary: Review the live preview | The carousel on the left shows sample screens using your current settings, updating in real time as you change them. Use it to confirm text is readable and spacing looks right before you commit — fixing the theme now is far faster than editing every…

title: Style the option and product cards
summary: Style the option and product cards | These controls style the tappable cards visitors choose from. Checkbox Kind sets circle or square selection markers, List Border Radius rounds the card corners (0 = sharp, 32 = very rounded; around 12 looks modern), and Item Title and Item…

title: Keep it reusable
summary: Keep it reusable | Prefer a theme that can cover every planned screen type rather than optimizing only for the first screen. You can fine-tune everything in the next step.

title: Pick the visual baseline
summary: Pick the visual baseline | Click a theme card to set it as the baseline for colors, fonts, spacing, and screen layouts. The selected card is highlighted and becomes the starting point for the Customize step.

title: Choose the checkout experience
summary: Choose the checkout experience | Pick how the payment form appears. An embedded form slides up as a bottom sheet and keeps visitors inside your funnel — recommended for most funnels since staying in-flow converts better. A full-page Stripe Checkout redirect is simpler to set up…

title: Add a description (optional)
summary: Add a description (optional) | Optionally add supporting text shown on the paywall and inside the Studio to spell out what's included, the key benefits, or the terms. Leave it blank if the product name already says everything a buyer needs to know.

title: Name the product
summary: Name the product | Set the display name customers see on the paywall and at checkout — this field is required. Use clear, benefit-focused wording like 'Premium Annual Plan' rather than an internal code or SKU, since this is part of the buying decision.

title: Choose the product type
summary: Choose the product type | Select subscription (recurring, billed on a schedule) or one-time payment (charged once). This decides which trial and subscription options appear below and which Stripe prices are eligible. If you change it after a live product is already wired up,…

title: Select Stripe mode
summary: Select Stripe mode | Choose whether this product uses your Test or Live Stripe credentials. Test mode lets you rehearse the whole checkout with no real charge; Live charges real customers. It has to match your connected Stripe mode and the mode you publish in — if they don't…

title: Add optional multi-currency pricing
summary: Add optional multi-currency pricing | Optionally add up to five extra currencies with their own amounts so international visitors see prices in their local money, which lifts conversion. At checkout Segmently shows the local price when one is defined for the visitor's currency;…

title: Set the amount and primary currency
summary: Set the amount and primary currency | Enter the base price and currency (USD, EUR, GBP, RUB) customers are charged at checkout. Type it in whole currency units — enter 9.99 for nine dollars ninety-nine, not 999. This value is sent to Stripe and shown to customers, so…

title: Set the price type and recurrence
summary: Set the price type and recurrence | Choose one-time (charged once) or recurring (billed on a schedule). For recurring, set the interval (day, week, month, year) and the count: count 1 bills every period, count 3 bills every third period — so interval 'month' + count 3 equals…

title: Select or create the Stripe price
summary: Select or create the Stripe price | Pick the exact price customers will be charged — this is what actually drives checkout, so if you leave the price empty the paywall will fail when a visitor tries to pay. The list filters to recurring prices for subscriptions and one-time…

title: Select or create the Stripe product
summary: Select or create the Stripe product | Link this paywall product to a real product in your Stripe account, or click to create one inline without leaving this dialog. It has to live in the same Stripe mode (Test or Live) you selected above — if it's in the other mode it won't…

title: Set the billing interval
summary: Set the billing interval | Choose how often customers are billed (daily, weekly, monthly, yearly) and the Every-X count for multi-period billing — for example every 3 months. This has to match the recurrence on the Stripe price you mapped, or Stripe will reject the checkout.

title: Configure the free trial
summary: Configure the free trial | Set how many free days a customer gets before the first charge; enter 0 for no trial. Billing starts the day after the trial ends. Always state the trial length clearly on the paywall — it keeps checkout compliant and cuts down on disputes and…

title: Charge an upfront fee at sign-up (optional)
summary: Charge an upfront fee at sign-up (optional) | Turn this on to charge a one-time fee the moment the subscription starts, on top of the recurring price — useful for an activation or onboarding fee. Leave it off for a standard free-trial or pay-as-you-go subscription. (This is…

title: Select the upfront fee price
summary: Select the upfront fee price | Pick or create the one-time Stripe price used for that upfront fee. It's charged immediately and billed separately from the recurring subscription, so it shows up as its own line in Stripe.

title: Keep test and live separate
summary: Keep test and live separate | Use test products for sandbox flows and live products for production flows. Mixing modes is the most common reason checkout setup fails.

title: Create products before attaching them
summary: Create products before attaching them | Paywall screens can only sell products that exist here, and every product must match the Stripe mode of the published flow. Create, edit, and delete products from this page.

title: Switch between Test and Live catalogs
summary: Switch between Test and Live catalogs | The Test and Live tabs hold two completely separate product catalogs, each with its own count badge. Start in Test while you're still validating — it can't charge real cards. Always glance at which tab is selected before you create or…

title: Keep the mode consistent everywhere
summary: Keep the mode consistent everywhere | A product only works at checkout if the paywall screen, your Stripe connection, and this tab are all in the same mode. A real launch needs a Live product with a Live Stripe connection; a safe rehearsal needs a Test product with a Test…

title: Understand button layout
summary: Understand button layout | Buttons stack vertically or horizontally based on width and theme, with the primary always before the secondary. Layout is automatic, so focus on labels and styling.

title: Set the primary button label
summary: Set the primary button label | The primary button text is the visible call-to-action (Continue, Next, Subscribe). Make it reflect the screen goal so visitors know what happens on click.

title: Style the primary button
summary: Style the primary button | Apply text and button styling through five accordion groups: Container (padding), Gradient, Shadow, Effects, and Icon. Strong styling makes the button read as the important next step.

title: Control primary button visibility
summary: Control primary button visibility | Toggle the primary button on or off. Hide it when visitors must interact with the content first; at least one of the primary or secondary buttons must stay visible.

title: Add an optional secondary button
summary: Add an optional secondary button | Enable and label a secondary action (Skip, Learn More, Log In) for an alternative path. Keep it less prominent than the primary; use it for exits, not the main goal.

title: Style the secondary button
summary: Style the secondary button | Style the secondary button with the same five accordion groups but lower visual priority (softer colors, lighter weight) to preserve the hierarchy.

title: Control secondary button visibility
summary: Control secondary button visibility | When the secondary button is enabled, toggle it visible or hidden. Hide it to force commitment to the primary action only.

title: Navigate the right panel
summary: Navigate the right panel | The right panel is a set of collapsible sections in screen-type order. Expand each accordion to reach its controls; text, styles, translations, and behavior are grouped within their section.

title: Work in the recommended order
summary: Work in the recommended order | Configure top to bottom: Header, Content, Options or Media, Action Bar, Background, then Basic Config. This order follows the visitor flow from orientation to visual treatment.

title: Understand shared vs unique sections
summary: Understand shared vs unique sections | Shared sections (Header, Action Bar, Backdrop, Basic Config) repeat across screen types; unique sections like Media, Options, or Text Field appear only where the type needs them. Know which sections your screen exposes.

title: Bind variables on selection screens
summary: Bind variables on selection screens | Selection screens (list, grid, text input, wheel picker) expose a Variable Binding section. Create or pick a flow variable, map items to options, and set score effects to influence later routing.

title: Connect your live Stripe account
summary: Connect your live Stripe account | Use Connect Live Account to authorize your production account. Live mode processes real payments and maps to your production products and prices, so connect it only after test validation is complete.

title: Verify live account readiness
summary: Verify live account readiness | Confirm that both charges and payouts are enabled before deploying a paywall to production. Finish any remaining business verification (identity, bank account) in the Stripe Dashboard if onboarding is incomplete.

title: Keep test and live separate
summary: Keep test and live separate | Test and live modes are independent and cannot be mixed in one published funnel. Every product in a single publish must use the same mode, so review the product mode before publishing to production.

title: Know what you are granting
summary: Know what you are granting | OAuth authorizes Segmently to read your products and prices and to create new ones inline in the product dialog. You are not granting direct charge access; all charges run through your connected Stripe account.

title: If products do not appear
summary: If products do not appear | If your Stripe products or prices are missing in the picker, verify you selected the matching mode and that the products exist in that Stripe account, since test and live are separate catalogs. Refresh the page or reconnect OAuth if needed.

title: Why test and live need separate connections
summary: Why test and live need separate connections | Stripe Connect Standard accounts require separate OAuth connections for test and live because each mode has its own account ID and API keys. This is a Stripe limitation; connecting test first is the recommended safe pattern.

title: Connect a test Stripe account
summary: Connect a test Stripe account | Use Connect Test Account to authorize Segmently for your test Stripe account. Test mode uses sandbox cards (for example 4242 4242 4242 4242) and never charges real customers, so validate products and checkout here first.

title: Check the test account status
summary: Check the test account status | After connecting, confirm the account shows charges enabled. If onboarding is incomplete, finish it in the Stripe Dashboard; you cannot create products or test checkout until charges are enabled.

title: Add an entry screen rule
summary: Add an entry screen rule | Open the form to create a routing rule. Each rule matches a URL parameter value and routes the visitor to a start screen; rules are checked top to bottom and the first match wins.

title: Remove a rule
summary: Remove a rule | Delete a rule permanently; this cannot be undone. With no matching rule, the default start screen is used.

title: Specify the value to match
summary: Specify the value to match | Enter the exact value the parameter must have to trigger the rule. The match is case-sensitive (for example, enter summer for utm_campaign=summer).

title: Choose the URL parameter to match
summary: Choose the URL parameter to match | Select a parameter you defined in Sources. Its key is read from the incoming URL (for example utm_campaign) when the funnel loads.

title: Choose the start screen
summary: Choose the start screen | Pick the V2 step where matching visitors land; it must exist in the selected onboarding version. Saved visitor progress overrides rules.

title: Enable or disable the rule
summary: Enable or disable the rule | Toggle a rule active or inactive. Disabled rules are kept but skipped at load, which is useful for testing or temporary pauses.

title: Find the Cloud URL
summary: Find the Cloud URL | This is the live public URL of the published funnel, using your custom domain when configured. Share it in ads, emails, and landing pages.

title: Copy the URL
summary: Copy the URL | Copy the Cloud URL to the clipboard for campaigns and links. The button shows a checkmark to confirm the copy.

title: Test locally with the Debug Panel (dev only)
summary: Test locally with the Debug Panel (dev only) | On localhost, a local URL with the Debug Panel shows live variable inspection, analytics preview, and error logs. Use it for QA before release.

title: Open the funnel in a new tab
summary: Open the funnel in a new tab | Open the Cloud URL to confirm it loads before sending traffic. It runs with full analytics and Stripe checkout.

title: Complete a smoke test
summary: Complete a smoke test | Open the Cloud URL in a clean (incognito) session, complete the flow, confirm analytics events fire, and test the paywall or checkout before sending traffic.

title: Why attach metadata, and how to add one

title: Watch the keys limit
summary: Watch the keys limit | A counter shows how many of Stripe's 50 metadata keys you've used. The Add button turns off once you hit the limit, so if you need room for a new field, remove a mapping you no longer need first.

title: Review the metadata preview
summary: Review the metadata preview | The JSON preview shows exactly how your chosen parameters will appear on the payment in Stripe. Check the field names and values here before saving, so your revenue reporting and reconciliation line up with the right campaign or source data.

title: Remove a parameter
summary: Remove a parameter | Delete a mapping to stop sending that field to Stripe on future payments. This only removes the mapping on this screen — it does not delete or change the parameter definition itself over in Sources.

title: Choose which parameter to send
summary: Choose which parameter to send | Select from the parameters you've already defined in Sources. The parameter's internal key becomes the field name shown in Stripe, and every value is sent to Stripe as plain text (a string), even numbers.
